Documentation → Devices & Lifecycle → Capacity Limits

Capacity Limits

Per model and firmware, record how many server policies, protection profiles, certificates and SNI policies a FortiWeb can hold, and set your own safety cap that clone workflows and device health check before objects are created.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb or FortiADC ADOM → Administrator → Capacity Limits (URL /capacity/)

What is it?#

Capacity Limits is the catalog of how many objects of each kind a FortiWeb model can hold on a given firmware version. For each object type you enter Fortinet's published ceiling (the hard max) and, optionally, your own lower operational cap. SATOM's clone workflows check this catalog before they create objects, and device health grades how close each appliance is to it.

What does it do?#

  • Keeps one row per model × firmware major × object type. The object types are:
  • Server Policies
  • Web Protection Profiles (inline and offline profiles together)
  • Local Certificates
  • SNI Policies
  • Computes the effective cap = the lower of the hard max and your operational cap.
  • Shows In use (fleet max): the highest count of that object type on any visible appliance of the same model and firmware major. The value is highlighted when it reaches the capacity warning level of the effective cap — the product's warning % from the monitoring thresholds settings (default 80 %).
  • Suggests fleet models that have no catalog yet, with a one-click add button.
  • Is checked by:
  • the clone/migrate pre-flight checklist of a server policy (headroom for one more server policy on the destination — see Policy cloning);
  • the clone and re-bind of a Web Protection Profile from Exceptions and Attack search (one more profile up front, then every object type of the whole clone plan before anything is written);
  • Device health, which grades each object type against the effective cap.

Requirements#

  • The appliance's Model and Firmware must be known in Appliances. SATOM matches a catalog by the exact model string and the firmware major (7.6.8 → 7.6). An appliance without a model or a parseable firmware has no catalog.
  • Counts come from SATOM's local cache of the appliance's objects, so the appliance must have been synchronised at least once.

Permissions#

All routes (view, add, save, delete) require users.manage (Administrator). Without it, /capacity/ answers 403, and the menu entry is not shown (the Administrator menu group is drawn only for users.manage).

Where it is reachable. The menu entry Capacity Limits is in the Administrator group of the FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs. The URL also opens in the Global, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs. The catalog shown is scoped to the active ADOM's product: each product ADOM shows its own product's catalogs, Global shows every product's.

How to use#

Add a model#

  1. Open Administrator → Capacity Limits.
  2. If the blue bar Fleet models without a limits catalog: lists your model, press its ＋ (, ) button. Otherwise enter Model / SKU (e.g. FortiWeb-VM02, FWB-600F), pick the Product (in a product ADOM only that product is offered; Global offers every product) and enter the Firmware major (for example 7.6), then press Add model.
  3. A card for the model appears with one empty row per object type.

💡Tip

Type the model exactly as it appears on the appliance in Appliances. A catalog only applies to appliances whose model string and firmware major match it.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Add model records the catalog for the product you pick (it used to always create FortiWeb rows), Remove only removes that product's rows, the in-use highlight follows your configured warning level, and the validation messages match the checks.

Set the limits#

  1. In the model's card, for each object type: - enter Hard max (Fortinet) — the ceiling from the model's datasheet; - choose a Cap mode: no cap, number or % of max; - enter the Cap value (an absolute number, or a percentage of the hard max).
  2. Press Save ().
  3. Check Effective cap — the number automations will respect.

Remove a model#

  1. Press the red trash button in the model's card header.
  2. Confirm "Remove ALL limit rows for ()?".

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Model / SKU Appliance model string Yes (add) FortiWeb-VM04
Product Product the catalog is for; only the products the active ADOM can create are offered Yes (add) FortiWeb
Firmware major Major.minor firmware version Yes (add) 7.6
Hard max (Fortinet) Published ceiling; whole number ≥ 0. Blank = unknown No 2000
Cap mode no cap — only the hard max applies; number — absolute cap; % of max — percentage of the hard max No % of max
Cap value For number: whole number ≥ 0, not above the hard max. For % of max: greater than 0 and at most 100 No 80
Effective cap Calculated: the lowest of hard max, number cap and hard max × percent ÷ 100 (rounded down) — 1600
Updated Who saved the row last, and when — admin 2026-01-15
  • With % of max and no hard max, there is no effective cap.
  • With number and no hard max, the number is the effective cap.
  • Choosing no cap (or leaving the value blank) clears the operational cap.

Example#

🧪Example — Keep 20 % head-room on a VM04

Your FortiWeb-VM04 appliances run firmware 7.6.x. The datasheet allows 2,000 server policies.

Object type Hard max Cap mode Cap value Effective cap
Server Policies 2000 % of max 80 1600

A colleague later clones a policy onto fweb-01 (a VM04 on 7.6.8) that already holds 1,600 server policies. The pre-flight checklist blocks the clone with "Capacity limit reached for Server Policies on fweb-01: used 1600 + 1 would exceed cap 1600 (hard max 2000)."

Result#

  • Saving updates only rows that changed and stamps them with your user name; the page shows "Saved limit row(s)." or "No changes.".
  • The Audit log records capacity.model_add, capacity.limits_update and capacity.model_delete.
  • From then on:
  • a clone that would exceed the effective cap is blocked with "Capacity limit reached for on : used + would exceed cap (hard max ).";
  • an object type with no cap set never blocks work — the check passes with "No capacity limit set for / ; allowing (used=).";
  • a whole-plan clone check lists object types that have no capped type at all as unchecked, instead of reporting them as verified;
  • Device health shows each object type as ok / warn / crit by percentage of the effective cap (thresholds from the monitoring thresholds settings; defaults 80 % and 95 %), and as no cap when none is set — which is reported as unknown, not healthy.

Troubleshooting#

"Model and firmware major are both required."#

Possible causes - Add model was pressed with an empty field.

Solution 1. Fill in both Model / SKU and Firmware major and press Add model again.

Verification - A card for the model appears with "Added (, ) — object types ready to configure."

"This ADOM cannot add capacity rows for ."#

Possible causes - The posted product is not one the active ADOM can create (a product ADOM can only add its own product).

Solution 1. Switch to that product's ADOM, or to Global, and add the model there.

Verification - The card shows the product next to the model name.
